surfaces.part: paddy ground tile (full 16x16 tile of textured golden-green terrain with a dark soil band at rows 1-2)

answer.evidence: The object is a full-bleed 16x16 terrain tile: every row is 16 px wide, with a dark brown soil/shadow band at rows 1-2 and a mottled golden-olive field texture across rows 3-15. The column scan shows only texture variation (L 117-208) with no front-edge line, no eave shadow, and no ellipse. It is a flat ground texture rather than a standing object, so it has no distinct top and front face. This is consistent with the terrain kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders as a very small golden straw patch with a dark brown bank strip along the top. The measured facts are 12 colours in the whole piece, against 80 for the grass reference. The 12 colours per tile are above the paving reference (7) but well under the grass (26), which is the closer match for a natural soil or grass surface. I count about 3-4 lightness steps on the golden body, against 5-6 in the references. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral and look brown, so the outline is a tinted material tone, not a black sticker line. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, and there is some vertical stalk striping, but it is regular and sparse. It lacks the clumped, multi-tone variation of the grass reference. A 4x3 paddy ground should carry far more grain, stubble and tonal variation across its tiles. With only 12 colours in total, it looks thinner and flatter than the references, so it fails.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the grass reference, and a median of 12 colours per tile against 26 for grass. It is only slightly above the paving reference, which is itself a sparse, low-colour piece. The candidate is tiny and reads as a single bank strip with a darker brown cap and a sandy-yellow body with horizontal striping. It does not read as a 4x3 paddy ground patch. Each ramp shows about 3 lightness steps (dark brown cap, mid, light sand), against 5-6 in the Beodeul grass, which has clumps in several greens plus tufts and highlights. Overall the shading is shallow and the variety is far below the reference. A careful artist would not accept it next to the grass tile.
